title: Inheritance shares that exceed the estate: Quran 4:11-12 and the 'awl fix
claim: Quran 4:11-12 and 4:176 assign fixed inheritance fractions, and in common cases they add up to more than the estate. A man leaving a wife, two daughters, and both parents yields 1/8 + 2/3 + 1/3 = 27/24. A man leaving a mother, wife, and two sisters yields 1/3 + 1/4 + 2/3 = 15/12. Islamic jurisprudence itself acknowledges the oversubscription: the doctrine of 'awl (proportional reduction of all shares) was invented to handle it — and by IslamQA's own account, no case of 'awl arose under Muhammad or Abu Bakr; the caliph Umar was the first to rule on it, meaning the Quran's 'perfectly detailed' law (6:114) required a human patch within a decade of Muhammad's death. A book claiming divine authorship and mathematical precision in its most legally binding passages should not need companions to renormalize its fractions.

sources.name: Answering Islam — Contradictions in the Qur'an (inheritance)
IslamOnline — Do Qur'anic inheritance rules involve mathematical errors?

response: Muslim jurists respond that the verses assign shares, not a summed distribution formula: when shares oversubscribe, 'awl preserves each heir's proportion relative to the others, which they argue is the intended design — a ratio system, not an addition problem. IslamOnline argues the internal proportions remain exactly as stated even when the denominators are scaled, so no mathematical error exists. IslamQA adds that the companions' consensus on 'awl demonstrates the system's flexibility rather than a defect, and that the Quran never promises the fractions sum to one in every configuration.
rationale: The controlling facts are conceded on the Islamic side: the fractions do exceed the estate in ordinary cases, and 'awl was a post-Muhammad juristic invention first ruled on by Umar — IslamQA states this plainly. The dispute is only over characterization ('ratios, not sums'). But the verses read as direct commands about actual portions of actual estates, closing with 'an obligation from Allah' (4:11), and the ratio defense is nowhere in the text — it was reverse-engineered after real estates came up short. Graded admitted rather than unrefuted because the substance (shares oversubscribe; humans patched it) is affirmed by Islamic jurisprudence itself.

title: Banu Qurayza: the mass execution Muhammad presided over
claim: In 627 AD, after the Battle of the Trench, the Jewish tribe Banu Qurayza surrendered to Muhammad. Sa'd ibn Mu'adh ruled that 'their warriors be killed and their children taken captive,' and Muhammad endorsed the verdict as 'the judgment of Allah' (Sahih al-Bukhari 3043). Ibn Ishaq's sira records 600–900 males beheaded in trenches dug in Medina's market, with Muhammad present; the women and children were enslaved and Muhammad took Rayhana from among the captives. Adulthood was determined by pubic-hair inspection — the survivor Atiyya al-Qurazi testifies to this directly (Sunan Abi Dawud 4404). These are not enemy accusations; every detail comes from Islam's own canonical hadith and earliest biography. The evangelistic contrast is stark: the test 'by their fruits you will know them' (Matthew 7:15-20) applied to the man Muslims must take as al-insan al-kamil, the perfect model (Quran 33:21).

sources.name: M. J. Kister — 'The Massacre of the Banu Qurayza' (Hebrew University)
WikiIslam — The Massacre of the Banu Qurayzah
Guillaume, The Life of Muhammad (Ibn Ishaq translation)

response: Muslim scholars answer that Banu Qurayza committed high treason during an existential siege, breaking their defense pact by negotiating with the attacking confederates; the penalty was wartime justice for treachery, not religious persecution. The verdict was delivered by Sa'd, an arbitrator the tribe itself accepted, and — as SeekersGuidance argues — matched the tribe's own law in Deuteronomy 20:10-14 for a besieged treacherous city. Some modern academics (following W. N. Arafat) also dispute the 600-900 figure as an exaggeration absorbed from Jewish narrators, arguing only the guilty leaders were executed.

responseSource.name: SeekersGuidance — A Balanced Explanation of the Banu Qurayza Controversy

rationale: The event itself is not denied by mainstream Islam — the defenses justify it. Bukhari preserves the judgment and Muhammad's endorsement; Abu Dawud preserves the puberty inspections; the sira supplies the scale. The Deuteronomy 20 parallel fails on its own terms (that law addressed distant cities in Israel's unique theocratic conquest, was never a standing model, and Muhammad claimed a universal, final revelation of mercy, 21:107). The Arafat revisionist number is rejected by Kister's classic study and sits awkwardly with the sahih material. What remains conceded on all sides: mass execution of surrendered prisoners, enslavement of their families, and the executor held up as humanity's perfect example.

title: Is Muhammad in the Bible? Deuteronomy 18, the Paraclete, and Song of Songs 5:16
claim: The Quran stakes its credibility on Muhammad being 'written in the Torah and the Gospel' (7:157) and on Jesus foretelling 'a messenger after me whose name is Ahmad' (61:6). The three standard proof-texts all fail on inspection. Deuteronomy 18:15-18 requires a prophet 'from among your brothers' — the Israelites (Deut 18:2 uses 'brothers' of fellow tribes) — who is like Moses; Acts 3:22 identifies him as Jesus, and Muhammad, a non-Israelite who mediated no covenant and per Islam performed no confirming signs, does not fit. The Paraclete of John 14-16 is 'the Spirit of truth,' whom 'the world cannot see,' who 'will be in you' and whom the disciples themselves would receive — impossible for a man born five centuries later; the periklytos conjecture has zero manuscript support. Song of Songs 5:16's 'machamaddim' is a common noun ('altogether desirable,' plural), used of the Shulamite's beloved, not a name. The dilemma bites both ways: if the Bible was corrupted, why does the Quran send Muslims to it to find Muhammad?

sources.name: Answering Islam — Deuteronomy 18:18: a prophecy of Muhammad?
Christian Research Institute — Muhammad and Deuteronomy 18
Apologetics Press — Does Song of Solomon Mention Muhammad?
Answering Muslims (David Wood) — Deuteronomy 18:18, reply to Zakir Naik

response: Dawah apologists (Deedat, Naik, Discover The Truth) argue: 'brothers' of the Israelites means their kin the Ishmaelites; Muhammad parallels Moses more closely than Jesus does (natural birth, marriage, lawgiving, migration, military leadership, natural death — points where Jesus, as divine Son, differs); the Paraclete passages were altered, or parakletos corrupts an original periklytos ('praised one' = Ahmad); and machamaddim is the very consonantal root of Muhammad's name appearing in a messianic love-song. They add that Quran 7:157 is corroborated precisely because traces survive despite centuries of textual transmission by hostile communities.

responseSource.name: Discover The Truth — Song of Songs 5:16 prophesied Muhammad

rationale: The Christian rebuttal stands essentially unanswered on the textual level. Deuteronomy 18:2 and 17:15 fix 'brothers' as Israelites; Deuteronomy 34:10-12 defines 'like Moses' by signs, wonders, and knowing God face to face — the exact credentials Islam denies Muhammad (Quran 29:50-51). Every Greek manuscript of John reads parakletos; the periklytos emendation is pure conjecture. Machamaddim is standard Hebrew vocabulary (also 2:3; Hosea 9:16). Most decisively, the argument self-destructs: 7:157 presupposes a readable, reliable Torah and Gospel in the 7th century — feeding directly into the app's central tahrif dilemma. No Muslim response engages that circularity successfully.

title: Ishmael, Isaac, and the Kaaba: Islam's rewritten Abraham
claim: Islam's foundation story runs through Abraham: the covenant passes through Ishmael, Abraham and Ishmael built the Kaaba in Mecca (Quran 2:127; 3:96), and the near-sacrifice was of Ishmael. Genesis says the opposite: God establishes His everlasting covenant through Isaac, explicitly not Ishmael, though Ishmael is blessed (Genesis 17:19-21; 21:12), and the sacrifice is 'your son, your only son Isaac' at Moriah (22:2). Strikingly, the Quran never names the sacrificed son (37:100-107), and early Muslim exegesis was split — al-Tabari, Islam's greatest classical commentator, concluded from the Quran's own sequence that it was Isaac. No pre-Islamic source — biblical, Jewish, Greek, Roman, or archaeological — places Abraham within a thousand miles of Mecca, and Genesis locates Ishmael's line in Paran and Shur, in northwest Arabia/Sinai, not the Hijaz. The Islamic claim requires the Torah to be textually corrupted at exactly these points — which lands in the tahrif trap: the Quran affirms the Torah in Muhammad's hands, and the manuscripts predate him.

sources.name: Answering Islam (Shamoun) — Abraham and the Child of Sacrifice
Answering Islam — Rebuttal on the sacrifice of Abraham (documents Tabari's view)
Islamic Awareness — The Sacrifice of Abraham: Isaac or Ishmael?
Sahih al-Bukhari 3364 (Abraham, Hagar, and Mecca narrative)

response: Muslim apologists argue the Torah's 'your only son Isaac' betrays later Israelite editing — Ishmael was Abraham's only son for about fourteen years, so 'only son' fits him alone, and a scribe allegedly inserted Isaac's name. They read Genesis 21:21's Paran as extending to the Hijaz, connect Psalm 84:6's 'valley of Baca' with Bakkah/Mecca (Quran 3:96), and take Bukhari 3364's detailed Abraham-in-Mecca narrative as preserved true history. Islamic Awareness contends the Quran's silence on the son's name is deliberate universality, and that the later consensus for Ishmael rests on sound reasoning from Quran 37's sequence of events.

responseSource.name: Islamic Awareness — The Sacrifice of Abraham

rationale: Every leg of the Muslim case depends on assuming Genesis corruption without manuscript evidence — and the Dead Sea Scrolls and Septuagint carry Genesis 17 and 22 unchanged from centuries before Christ, let alone Muhammad. The 'only son' argument concedes the method: rewrite the text to fit the claim. Tabari's verdict for Isaac shows even Islam's classical scholarship could not read Ishmael out of Quran 37. Paran is fixed by Genesis 14:6 and Numbers 10-13 near Sinai; Baca is a valley en route to Zion (Psalm 84:7). No pre-Islamic trace of an Abrahamic Kaaba exists. The claim survives only inside the tahrif assumption the app's core dilemma already dismantles.

title: The rabbis' commentary in Allah's voice: Sanhedrin 4:5, the Seven Sleepers, and Abraham's furnace
claim: Several Quranic narratives track post-biblical Jewish and Christian legends, not the Bible. Quran 5:32 — 'whoever kills a soul... it is as if he killed all mankind' — reproduces Mishnah Sanhedrin 4:5, a rabbinic homily on Cain composed centuries before Islam, and even keeps its Israel-specific framing ('We decreed upon the Children of Israel'). The preceding verse's raven who shows Cain how to bury Abel (5:31) parallels the same midrashic cluster. Quran 18:9-26 retells the Seven Sleepers of Ephesus — a Christian legend attested in Jacob of Serugh (d. 521) and Gregory of Tours — complete with the dog and the disputed head-count, presented as revelation about real 'youths of the cave.' Quran 21:68-69 has Abraham thrown into a fire, a story that arose from Genesis Rabbah's wordplay reading 'Ur' of the Chaldees as ur, 'fire.' A book delivering eternal truth should not canonize identifiable human commentary, folklore, and a pun as history.

sources.name: Gilchrist — Other Qur'anic Origins and Sources
WikiIslam — Seven Sleepers of Ephesus in the Quran
Wikipedia — List of legends in the Quran

response: Islamic Awareness and similar apologists respond on three fronts: parallel does not prove borrowing — a common divine source or shared true history explains overlap; some alleged sources (e.g., Pirke de-Rabbi Eliezer for the raven) may postdate Islam, reversing the borrowing; and the Quran self-consciously corrects and reframes these accounts (on the Sleepers, 18:22 rebukes speculation about the number, showing critical engagement, not credulous copying). On 5:32, they argue Allah confirming a truth He originally inspired to Israel's sages is no embarrassment — the verse explicitly says the decree was given to the Children of Israel.

responseSource.name: Islamic Awareness — Sources of the Qur'an (responses)

rationale: The dating defense fails where it matters most: Mishnah Sanhedrin was redacted c. 200 AD, Genesis Rabbah by the 5th century, and the Seven Sleepers is firmly pre-Islamic in Jacob of Serugh — these three are secure, whatever one says about Pirke de-Rabbi Eliezer. The 'divine confirmation' move cannot rescue 5:32, because what the Quran presents as Allah's decree is identifiably a rabbi's exegetical inference from Hebrew grammar ('bloods of your brother'), and the Sleepers is a legend about the reign of Decius, not scripture. The 18:22 'correction' concedes the story arrived as circulating folklore. No Muslim response explains why revelation reproduces commentary.

title: Seventy-two houris: the carnal paradise versus the presence of God
claim: The Quran's paradise is insistently sensual: wide-eyed maidens 'whom no man or jinn has touched' (55:56, 74), virgins made 'devoted, of equal age' for the companions of the right (56:35-38), 'full-breasted maidens of equal age' (78:33, kawa'ib atraban), wine, couches, and served boys. The hadith intensify it: the martyr is 'married to seventy-two wives among the houris' (Jami at-Tirmidhi 1663, graded hasan sahih by Tirmidhi), and each man receives wives with marrow visible through their flesh in a pearl tent sixty miles wide (Sahih al-Bukhari 3243). IslamQA affirms the houris as literal wives given for sexual enjoyment. Jesus taught the opposite: in the resurrection 'they neither marry nor are given in marriage' (Matthew 22:30), and heaven's center is God Himself dwelling with His people (Revelation 21:3; 22:4). The contrast exposes what each faith holds as the ultimate good — reward, or God.

sources.name: Mufti of Federal Territory (Malaysia) — status of the 72-wives hadith

response: Muslim scholars reply that critics caricature paradise: the Quran itself says 'the pleasure of Allah is greater' than all of it (9:72), and sound hadith make the beatific vision of Allah's Face the supreme reward. Physical delights are real because humans are resurrected bodily — a point Christianity shares (a wedding feast, a city, a renewed earth) — and purified of sin ('no idle talk therein,' 56:25). The 72 number specifically comes from a single companion-chain some scholars grade weaker, and translations like 'full-breasted' are contested renderings of kawa'ib. Believing wives, they note, are promised higher status than the houris.
rationale: This is graded admitted because mainstream Islamic authority affirms the substance: IslamQA and classical tafsir teach literal houris as sexual companions, and Tirmidhi himself graded the 72-wives hadith hasan sahih. The 9:72 rejoinder is fair as far as it goes — Islam does hold Allah's pleasure supreme — but it does not erase that the Quran's dominant, repeated portrait of reward is virgins, couches, and wine, while God's own presence with His people, the engine of biblical hope from Eden to Revelation, is structurally marginal. The evangelistic point stands on Islam's own affirmed doctrine, not on polemical exaggeration.

title: Half a witness, half an heir: women's legal standing in Islam's own texts
claim: Quran 2:282 requires two women to replace one male witness 'so that if one errs, the other can remind her,' and 4:11 fixes a daughter's inheritance at half a son's. Muhammad drew the theological conclusion himself: 'Is not the witness of a woman equal to half that of a man?... This is because of the deficiency of a woman's mind' (Sahih al-Bukhari 2658), and in Bukhari 304 declares women 'deficient in intelligence and religion' and 'the majority of the dwellers of Hell-fire.' These are not fringe readings — classical fiqh built evidentiary and inheritance law on them, and they remain live in sharia codes today. Scripture's trajectory is different in kind: male and female are jointly God's image (Genesis 1:27), the risen Christ's first commissioned witnesses were women (Luke 24:9-11) — legally worthless testimony in that culture, preserved anyway — and in Christ 'there is no male and female' (Galatians 3:28).

sources.name: Wikipedia — Status of women's testimony in Islam
IslamQA 111867 — Meaning of the lack in reason and religion in women

response: IslamQA and classical commentators explain the 'deficiency' as domain-specific, not essential: the testimony rule concerns financial contracts women then rarely handled, so a second woman guards against inexperience-driven error; the religion 'deficiency' refers only to exemption from prayer and fasting during menstruation — an excused, not culpable, lack. Inheritance halves reflect economics, not worth: men bear mandatory financial responsibility for women (mahr, full family maintenance), so a sister's unencumbered half can exceed a brother's encumbered whole. Modern Muslim scholars add that 2:282 is context-bound commercial procedure, noting other testimony contexts where a woman's word stands alone (24:6-9).
rationale: The texts and their operative legal force are undisputed — the defenses reinterpret motive, not content. And the softening glosses collide with the sources themselves: Bukhari 2658 grounds the testimony rule in 'deficiency of mind,' not commercial inexperience, and the economics defense does not touch 'majority of the dwellers of Hell-fire.' Classical fiqh applied the half-witness rule far beyond finance, and states applying sharia apply it now. Because the substance is affirmed by Islam's most authentic hadith and mainstream fatwa bodies, this is admitted; the honest debate is only over whether the arrangement is demeaning, which the texts' own stated rationale settles.

title: Seventeen times a day: the Fatiha and 'those who earned wrath... those astray'
claim: Every observant Muslim recites Surah al-Fatiha in each unit of the five daily prayers — at minimum seventeen times daily — closing with a plea to be guided in the path of those God favored, 'not of those who have earned anger, nor of those who go astray' (1:7). Muhammad himself identified the referents: 'Those who have earned the anger are the Jews, and those who are led astray are the Christians' (Jami at-Tirmidhi 2954, graded hasan; from Adi ibn Hatim). Ibn Kathir records that 'the scholars of tafsir' held this view, citing broad early consensus, and it stands in Tafsir al-Jalalayn and mainstream Salafi teaching today. The world's second-largest religion thus liturgically defines itself, dozens of times a day, against Jews and Christians by name. Contrast the New Testament's posture toward those outside: 'love your enemies and pray for them' (Matthew 5:44) and Paul's 'my heart's desire and prayer to God for them is that they may be saved' (Romans 10:1).

sources.name: Troid (Salafi) — Tafsir of al-Fatiha: the misguided and those who earned anger

response: Many Muslim teachers argue the verse names categories, not ethnicities: 'those who earned anger' are all who know truth and abandon it, 'those astray' all who strive without knowledge — Jews and Christians appear in the hadith as historical exemplars, not exclusive targets, and Muslims who fit the descriptions are equally included. The prayer, they stress, is a positive petition for guidance, not a curse on anyone; nothing in it asks harm for Jews or Christians. Modern expositors (e.g., Najam Academy's treatment) note the Quran elsewhere commends righteous People of the Book (3:113-115), so 1:7 cannot be a blanket condemnation.

responseSource.name: Najam Academy — Who are 'those who have earned God's anger'?

rationale: The identification is Islam's own, from Muhammad's mouth in a hasan hadith, endorsed by Ibn Kathir as the view of 'the scholars of tafsir' — the categorical reading is the modern softening, not the classical mainstream. Graded admitted because the substance (the canonical exegesis names Jews and Christians) is affirmed within Islamic tradition itself; the defense that it is exemplary rather than exhaustive is genuine but does not remove Jews and Christians from the referent — it universalizes the condemnation while keeping them as its archetypes. For evangelism the point is posture: daily self-definition against the biblical communities versus daily intercession for the lost.

title: The hadith dilemma: Islam's own chain-of-custody problem
claim: Nearly everything Islam knows about Muhammad — how to pray, the five pillars' details, Aisha's age, the sira's events, the Quran's own compilation story — comes from hadith first written down generations after his death in 632. Bukhari (d. 870) reportedly sifted some 600,000 circulating reports and kept roughly 7,000 (with repetitions) as authentic — meaning the Muslim community itself generated fabrications on an industrial scale for two centuries. Western scholarship (Goldziher, Schacht, Juynboll) showed isnads were routinely improved and back-projected, with 'common links' suggesting many chains were fabricated wholesale. The dilemma for dawah: if hadith are unreliable, Islam cannot perform its own prayers, define its pillars, or narrate its prophet — and the Quran becomes an unmoored text with no context. If hadith are reliable, then Bukhari's reports — Aisha at nine, the bewitchment, Banu Qurayza, 'deficient in mind' — all stand. Meanwhile the Gospels were written within living memory of eyewitnesses, a fraction of the hadith gap.

sources.name: IlmGate — Analyzing Schacht's theory and two of his critiques (Azami, Motzki)
ResearchGate — Hadith, Law, and Orientalism: a critical study of Schacht
Jonathan Brown on historical criticism of Islamic primary texts

response: Muslim scholars answer that hadith science is history's most rigorous authentication system: transmitters were biographically vetted (ilm al-rijal), chains cross-checked, and mass-transmitted (mutawatir) reports are epistemically certain. Azami and Motzki showed Schacht's dating arguments overreach — early written records (sahifas of companions like Hammam ibn Munabbih) push documentation back near the eyewitness generation, and Motzki's isnad-cum-matn analysis authenticates material Schacht dismissed. Jonathan Brown argues the tradition itself catalogued fabrications and graded reports with a sophistication Western criticism only rediscovered. The 600,000 figure counts chain-variants, not distinct lies.

responseSource.name: IlmGate — Azami and Motzki vs. Schacht

rationale: The Muslim defense is serious scholarship, but it sharpens rather than escapes the dilemma — every rehabilitation of hadith reliability re-authenticates Bukhari's most damaging contents, which the same apologists elsewhere minimize. Conversely, every appeal to fabrication, context, or weak chains against those reports saws off the branch Islamic practice sits on. The asymmetry with the New Testament is quantitative and qualitative: 25-60 years versus 150-250, continuous written transmission versus memorized chains, and hostile-witness-checkable public events. As a structured dilemma — parallel to the app's tahrif centerpiece — it has no published Muslim resolution that keeps both consistency and orthodoxy.

title: Mariya, Hafsa, and Surah 66: an oath annulled by revelation
claim: Surah 66 opens with Allah rebuking Muhammad: 'O Prophet, why do you prohibit what Allah has made lawful for you, seeking the approval of your wives?' (66:1), then dissolves his oath (66:2) and warns his wives that if he divorces them Allah will give him better ones (66:5). Sunan an-Nasa'i 3959 — graded sahih by al-Albani — supplies the occasion: Muhammad 'had intercourse with' his slave woman (identified in tafsir as Mariya the Copt) in Hafsa's quarters or on her day; Aisha and Hafsa pressed him until he swore Mariya forbidden to himself, whereupon revelation descended freeing him from the oath. An alternative sahih occasion (Bukhari 4912) involves only honey. Either way the structure matches the Zaynab pattern the app already covers: heaven intervenes, promptly and specifically, to release Muhammad from a domestic bind and side with his desires — precisely what Aisha noted dryly ('your Lord hastens to fulfill your wishes').

sources.name: Ask Ghamidi — the Mariya narration discussed

response: Muslim scholars overwhelmingly prefer the honey account in Bukhari and Muslim as the surah's occasion: Aisha herself narrates a jealous scheme about a honey drink at Zaynab's house, and the strongest-authenticated report should fix the context. The Mariya narrations, they argue, are aberrant (shadhdh) or conflated later reconstructions, and even if some chain is technically sound, occasion-of-revelation reports are notoriously fluid. On the substance: the surah shows Muhammad's humanity and Allah's correction — he is rebuked, not indulged — and the principle established (one may not make the lawful unlawful by oath) is sober jurisprudence, with expiation prescribed (66:2), matching Quran 5:89.

responseSource.name: Ask Ghamidi — Narration on Mariya and Surah 66

rationale: Graded contested honestly: the honey narration is the better-attested occasion, and Christians should not overclaim the Mariya version — though al-Albani's sahih grading of Nasa'i 3959 means Muslims cannot simply wave it away either. But even on the most favorable Muslim reading, the pattern stands on the Quran's face: a chapter of eternal scripture devoted to Muhammad's harem friction, dissolving his oath, and threatening his wives with replacement (66:5). Combined with 33:37 and 33:50-51 (already in the app), it exhibits revelation repeatedly bending toward the prophet's personal convenience — the cumulative case, not the single incident, carries the evangelistic weight.

title: Safiyya of Khaybar: bride of the man who killed her husband — that week
claim: At Khaybar (628 AD), the Muslims killed Kinana ibn al-Rabi, husband of the seventeen-year-old Jewish noblewoman Safiyya bint Huyayy — Ibn Ishaq adds that Kinana was first tortured with fire to reveal treasure, then beheaded (Guillaume, p. 515). Her father had already been executed with Banu Qurayza. Safiyya was taken captive, initially allotted to Dihya al-Kalbi, then reassigned to Muhammad (Sahih al-Bukhari 4200). Sahih al-Bukhari 371 records that Muhammad consummated the marriage on the journey home, at Sidd as-Sahba, days after her husband's death — the companions wondering aloud whether she was wife or concubine. Islamic sources present this as honor; the plain sequence is: kill a woman's husband and father, and marry her within the week, with no possibility of free consent and the mourning-period (idda) rules set aside. Set this against the biblical prophet-test: 'by their fruits you will know them' (Matthew 7:16).

sources.name: Guillaume, The Life of Muhammad (Ibn Ishaq)
Answering Islam — Muhammad and Safiyya: disregarding the idda

response: Muslim writers respond that Safiyya was honored, not violated: Muhammad freed her, made emancipation her mahr, and elevated a captive to Mother of the Believers; later reports show her expressing love for him and defending him. Kinana died, they argue, for breaching Khaybar's surrender terms by hiding treasure — a treaty violation, with the torture detail resting on Ibn Ishaq's chainless report, not sahih hadith. Her marriage protected her from ordinary captivity in a world where a defeated noblewoman had no better outcome. The consummation followed her purification (istibra), satisfying the applicable waiting rule for captives, and Al Hakam argues her consent is explicitly recorded.

responseSource.name: Al Hakam — Did Muhammad force Safiyya into marriage?

rationale: The core sequence — husband killed at Khaybar, Safiyya taken from the captives, consummation on the return journey — is Bukhari, not polemic; only the torture detail depends on the sira alone. The defenses concede every load-bearing fact and reframe them as magnanimity. But 'consent' by a teenager whose husband and father the marrying party's forces killed, offered marriage or captivity, is not consent in any meaningful sense, and 'honor' presupposes the legitimacy of the captivity system itself (Quran 33:50). Graded admitted: Islamic sources affirm the substance, and the dispute is entirely over whether it was praiseworthy — which is precisely the character question the prophet-test category exists to pose.

title: Mut'ah: the temporary marriage Muhammad permitted
claim: Sahih hadith establish that Muhammad permitted mut'ah — marriage contracted for a fixed term and payment, dissolving automatically: companions on campaign were allowed to marry women 'for a fixed time' even for a garment (Sahih Muslim 1404), and Jabir reports the practice continued through Abu Bakr's reign until Umar banned it (Sahih Muslim 1405). Sunni Islam holds Muhammad finally prohibited it (Sahih al-Bukhari 5115; Sahih Muslim 1406 — 'Allah has forbidden it until the Day of Resurrection'), though the abrogation is variously dated to Khaybar, Mecca's conquest, or Umar's caliphate. Shia Islam rejects the abrogation, grounds the practice in Quran 4:24 ('give them their due compensation for what you have enjoyed'), and practices mut'ah today, where it functions in documented cases as religiously laundered prostitution. Either Muhammad sanctioned term-limited sexual contracts, or the community that transmitted his religion cannot agree on what he finally commanded — both horns matter evangelistically against 'a marriage covenant witnessed by God' (Malachi 2:14).

sources.name: Sahih Muslim — Book of Marriage (mut'ah reports)
Al-Islam.org (Shia) — Temporary marriage: evidences from Sunni hadith collections

response: Sunni scholars answer that mut'ah belongs to Islam's gradualist pedagogy, like the phased prohibition of alcohol: permitted briefly under wartime hardship, then abrogated by the Prophet himself 'until the Day of Resurrection' (Sahih Muslim 1406), with the four Sunni schools unanimous on its prohibition — so Islam cannot be charged with what it abolished. Umar's ban merely enforced the Prophet's ruling. Shia scholars answer the opposite: 4:24 sanctions it, no abrogating verse exists, and Umar had no authority to forbid what Muhammad allowed; regulated mut'ah, with dower, term, and idda, is a lawful institution, not prostitution.
rationale: Graded contested because the Sunni abrogation defense is a genuine, well-sourced internal answer — Bukhari and Muslim do record prohibition, and it would be unfair to charge Sunni Islam with a practice it anathematizes. But the challenge is not fully answered: Muhammad undeniably permitted term-limited sexual contracts for some period (both sects agree), which is itself the moral datum against the biblical vision of marriage; the abrogation chronology is internally tangled; and a quarter of the Muslim world's second-largest branch practices mut'ah now on Quranic grounds Sunnis cannot conclusively rebut without Umar's authority. The disagreement also feeds the hadith-epistemology entry: the two communities' canons yield opposite final rulings.

title: The Black Stone and the Kaaba: pre-Islamic rites retained
claim: Islam's central rites predate Islam. The Kaaba was a functioning pagan shrine housing 360 idols until Muhammad cleansed it in 630 (Sahih al-Bukhari 4287); pre-Islamic Arabs already performed tawaf, venerated the Black Stone, and ran between Safa and Marwa — a rite associated with the idols Isaf and Na'ila that the Quran had to expressly re-authorize (2:158). Muslims still kiss or salute the embedded Black Stone in the Kaaba's corner; Umar's famous unease is canonical: 'I know that you are a stone and can neither benefit nor harm. Had I not seen the Prophet kissing you, I would not have kissed you' (Sahih al-Bukhari 1597) — while other hadith give the stone quasi-magical properties: it descended from paradise whiter than milk, blackened by sins, and will testify on judgment day (Jami at-Tirmidhi 877, 961). The question for a faith that defines itself against idolatry: why does pure monotheism's holiest act incorporate a pagan sanctuary's stone-veneration circuit, unchanged in form?

sources.name: WikiIslam — Pre-Islamic Arab religion in Islam
Answering Islam — Stone kissing and idolatry

response: The Islamic answer is that the direction of history is reversed: Abraham and Ishmael built the Kaaba for pure monotheism (Quran 2:127), and the pagan rites were later corruptions of an originally Abrahamic pilgrimage — Islam did not adopt paganism; it stripped paganism off an ancient monotheist sanctuary and restored the original. Kissing the stone, IslamQA explains, is pure ittiba' (following the Prophet's example), explicitly not worship — Umar's statement is cited by Muslims themselves as proof the act carries no belief in the stone's power. Tawaf and Safa-Marwa commemorate Abrahamic history (Hagar's search for water), re-sanctified by revelation.

responseSource.name: IslamQA 118085 — Why do Muslims kiss the Black Stone?

rationale: Graded contested, conservatively. The continuity of the rites with pre-Islamic paganism is a matter of Islamic record (Bukhari 4287; the 2:158 re-authorization presupposes pagan association), and the 'Abrahamic original' has zero pre-Islamic evidentiary support — it depends wholly on the Quran's assertion, and the Ishmael entry shows Genesis places Abraham nowhere near Mecca. But the Muslim intent-distinction is real: mainstream Islam explicitly denies the stone any power, and Umar's canonical statement functions as an internal anti-idolatry guardrail. The strong claim 'Muslims worship a stone' fails; the fair claim — Islam's central rite is a retained pagan circuit resting on an unevidenced origin story — stands.

title: Surah 9 and the chronology problem: which verses are Islam's last word?
claim: Surah 9 — by Muslim consensus among the last revealed — commands: 'kill the polytheists wherever you find them' after the sacred months (9:5), and 'fight those who do not believe in Allah... from the People of the Book until they pay the jizya with willing submission, and feel themselves subdued' (9:29). Under Islam's own abrogation doctrine (2:106, already in the app), later revelation governs earlier: Ibn Kathir's tafsir records Ad-Dahhak's judgment that the 'Verse of the Sword' 'abrogated every agreement of peace between the Prophet and any idolator, every treaty, and every term.' Classical jurists across the schools built offensive-jihad doctrine on exactly this chronology, and Muhammad's own summary is canonical: 'I have been ordered to fight the people until they say: none has the right to be worshipped but Allah' (Sahih al-Bukhari 25). The frequently quoted 'no compulsion in religion' (2:256) is Medinan but earlier — which is why the classical tradition, not Islamophobes, treated the sword verses as operative. Jesus's final commands run the other direction: 'put your sword back' (Matthew 26:52); 'make disciples... teaching them' (Matthew 28:19-20).

sources.name: Discover The Truth — An historical examination of the Sword Verse (Muslim rebuttal)

response: Muslim scholars answer that context confines both verses: 9:1-4 addresses pagan tribes who violated their treaties — 9:4 explicitly exempts those who kept terms, and 9:6 commands escorting an enemy who seeks protection to safety; 9:29 concerns hostile Byzantine-aligned powers ahead of Tabuk, not all Christians everywhere. The sweeping abrogation claims are attributed to individual exegetes, not consensus; many classical and nearly all modern scholars hold 2:256 and 60:8 un-abrogated, making jihad defensive or state-conducted, never vigilante. Bukhari 25's 'the people' is read as the specific treaty-breaking Arab polytheists, per the parallel narrations.

responseSource.name: Discover The Truth — Sword Verse examination

rationale: Contested is the honest grade: the contextual defense has genuine textual anchors (9:4, 9:6), and painting all Islam with Ad-Dahhak's maximalism would be the mirror error of Muslim apologists' minimalism. What the defense cannot dissolve: 9:29 targets People of the Book as such, prescribing fighting until tribute and subjugation — a command classical fiqh of every school operationalized for a millennium of expansionist jurisprudence; the contextual reading is historically the reformist position, not the classical one. The evangelistic use is precise, not polemical: ask which trajectory each founder's final commands set — and note this entry deliberately complements, without duplicating, the app's sharia (#35) and spread-by-sword (#38) entries.

title: The bewitched prophet: Bukhari's magic spell and the reliability of revelation
claim: Sahih al-Bukhari 3268 — narrated by Aisha — reports that a Jewish sorcerer, Labid ibn al-A'sam, worked magic on Muhammad using his hair and a comb 'so that he began to imagine that he had done a thing which he had not really done,' a state lasting by some accounts months. Muslim (2189) carries the same account; it is as authenticated as hadith get. The problem is double. Internally: the Quran indignantly denies the charge that Muhammad was 'a bewitched man' (17:47; 25:8) — yet Islam's most authentic hadith affirm exactly that. Epistemically: a prophet whose mind could be made to experience things that never happened, by a hostile magician, for an extended period during his revelatory career, has no way to certify which of his experiences — including revelations — were genuine. The biblical test excludes this categorically: God's true prophet is not overpowered by sorcery ('there is no enchantment against Jacob,' Numbers 23:23), and God's word does not come through a compromised channel (Deuteronomy 18:21-22).

sources.name: IslamQA 68814 — The story of the magic and its meaning
SeekersGuidance — Was the Prophet affected by magic?

response: IslamQA and mainstream commentators respond that the magic affected only Muhammad's worldly, domestic life — classically, imagining he had approached his wives when he had not — and never touched revelation, whose integrity Allah guarantees (5:67; 15:9). It was an illness like any bodily ailment prophets suffer, it ended in a miracle (Allah revealed the spell's location and cure, per the hadith itself, with Surahs 113-114 linked to the deliverance), and 25:8's denial concerns the pagans' charge that the Quran itself was sorcery's product — a different claim from the prophet suffering a temporary spell. Some early scholars and modernists simply rejected the report as contradicting the Quran.
rationale: The 'worldly matters only' firewall is asserted, never demonstrated: the hadith's own description — believing he had done what he had not done — is a defect of perception and memory, the exact faculties revelation depends on, and no criterion is offered by which Muhammad or anyone else could partition bewitched experiences from genuine ones. The minority who reject the report to save the Quran (a live Muslim position) impale themselves on the hadith-epistemology dilemma: Bukhari's most rigorously authenticated Aisha material falls, and Islamic method falls with it. The internal tension with 25:8 is answered only by redescribing the pagans' charge. No resolution holds all three: sahih hadith, Quranic denial, prophetic reliability.

title: Islam's substitute: 'your ransom from the Fire — a Jew or a Christian'
claim: Sahih Muslim preserves a startling soteriology: 'When it is the Day of Resurrection, Allah will deliver to every Muslim a Jew or a Christian and say: That is your rescue from Hell-Fire' (Sahih Muslim 2767a). The companion narration is stronger still: Muslims will arrive 'with sins like mountains,' and Allah will forgive the Muslims 'and place them on the Jews and Christians' instead (2767c-d); 'No Muslim dies but Allah admits in his stead a Jew or a Christian in Hell-Fire' (2767b). This is substitutionary atonement inverted: the innocent-of-those-sins damned in place of the guilty, by ethnic-religious category, without consent, justice, or love. The gospel's substitution is its precise mirror: the sinless one voluntarily bears sin for the guilty — 'He himself bore our sins in his body on the tree' (1 Peter 2:24); 'the Lamb of God who takes away the sin of the world' (John 1:29). Every human heart senses guilt must go somewhere; the two religions answer with opposite substitutes.

sources.name: IslamQA 9488 — Meaning of the hadith about sins placed on the People of the Book
Answering Islam (Shamoun) — How will a Muslim be saved according to the hadiths?
Street Theologian — Christians: a Muslim's ransom from hell?

response: IslamQA explains that the unbelievers are not punished for the Muslims' sins — that would contradict 'no bearer of burdens bears the burden of another' (6:164). Rather, the Jew or Christian enters Hell for his own disbelief; 'ransom' (fida') is figurative: each person has a place in Paradise and a place in Hell, and when a Muslim is forgiven, the unbeliever 'inherits' the vacated place in Hell that his own sins already earned, as the Muslim inherits his place in Paradise (per the parallel in Muslim's collection). Al-Nawawi's commentary takes the wording as metaphor for the fixed populations of the two abodes, so no injustice occurs.
rationale: The hadith are sahih Muslim material and IslamQA's harmonization concedes the wording requires rescue: the 'inherited places' reading must flatly re-explain 'Allah would forgive the Muslims and place [their sins] on the Jews and Christians,' which states transfer, not vacancy. Even granting Nawawi's metaphor, the admitted picture remains: Muslims with mountain-sized sins are forgiven not through any atonement but by category membership, while Jews and Christians serve as their counterweight — mercy without a ground, at the expense of justice, precisely the problem the cross answers (Romans 3:26). Graded admitted since the texts and their canonical status are affirmed; only the mechanics are debated. Powerful, underused evangelistic bridge to substitution rightly understood.

title: 'The Jews say Ezra is the son of Allah' — a claim no Jew ever made
claim: Quran 9:30 asserts as fact: 'The Jews say: Ezra (Uzair) is the son of Allah' — parallel to the Christian confession of Christ — and pronounces Allah's curse on both groups for it. But no Jewish text, sect, or tradition in the entire historical record calls Ezra the son of God: not the Tanakh, Talmud, Mishnah, Philo, Josephus, Qumran, or any rabbinic source. Judaism's defining confession is the Shema (Deuteronomy 6:4), and deifying a scribe would be its ultimate blasphemy. Historians, as the standard literature concedes, find the verse 'enigmatic' precisely because the belief is unattested. The error matters doubly for dawah: first, an omniscient author does not misreport the theology of a community living in Medina alongside Muhammad; second, the verse's symmetry ('...and the Christians say the Messiah is the son of Allah') shows the Quran treating both sonship claims as parallel human inventions — misunderstanding the Christian claim it means to refute, as the app's sonship entries already document.

sources.name: Answering Islam — Was Uzayr (Ezra) called the Son of God?
IslamQA 164633 — A Jewish person rejecting what the Qur'an says about Uzayr

response: Muslim commentators from Tabari onward answer that the verse reports a claim of some Jews, not all: classical tafsir names individual Medinan Jews (e.g., Finhas) or a Yemeni or Arabian Jewish faction who venerated Ezra as restorer of the Torah to the point of calling him Allah's son; Arabic reportedly permits attributing a subgroup's saying to the group. The absence from surviving Jewish literature proves little, they argue, since a heterodox Arabian sect would leave no rabbinic paper trail — and some modern Muslim writers point to 4 Ezra's exalted Ezra, or the deified-scribe traditions around Enoch/Metatron, as the kind of milieu the Quran could be indicting.
rationale: The defense is an argument from silence about a sect for which the only evidence is the verse needing rescue — methodologically circular, and the classical commentators' mutually conflicting identifications (one man, one delegation, a Yemeni sect) show they possessed no actual historical referent. 4 Ezra and Metatron traditions never call Ezra God's son and belong to different figures and genres. The verse generalizes ('the Jews say') exactly as it does for Christians, where the Quran means the mainstream confession — so the subgroup reading is special pleading. As with the Mary-in-the-Trinity entry already in the app, the pattern is a polemicist's misreport of neighbors' beliefs, not omniscience.

title: 'Allah is a foreign god's name' — a polemic Christians should drop
claim: A popular evangelical polemic claims 'Allah' is intrinsically the name of a false deity, so Muslims linguistically worship someone other than the biblical God, and Christians must never use the word. The evidence is against the linguistic claim. 'Allah' is simply Arabic for 'God' (al-ilah, 'the God'), cognate with Hebrew Eloah/Elohim and Aramaic Alaha — likely close to what Jesus's own Aramaic-speaking circle called God. Arab Christians used it before Muhammad existed: the trilingual Zabad inscription (512 AD), on a church of St. Sergius, opens its Arabic line invoking al-ilah; pre-Islamic Christian Arab tribes prayed to Allah, and every Arabic Bible from the earliest translations to today renders 'God' as 'Allah' — millions of Arab Christians confess 'Allah' as Father, Son, and Holy Spirit every Sunday. The real issue is conceptual, not lexical: whether the Quran's characterization of God is true — which is the work of the app's doctrine-of-god entries, and it is not advanced by a false etymology argument.

sources.name: Islamic Awareness — The Zebed inscription (512 CE)
ResearchGate — Allah, Al-Ilah, and Allahumma: Arabic usage before the 9th century
Sidney Griffith — The Church in the Shadow of the Mosque (Princeton UP)

response: Muslim apologists happily agree with the linguistic facts and press them further: since Allah is the God of Abraham by name and heritage, and Quran 29:46 instructs Muslims to tell the People of the Book 'our God and your God is one,' Christians who concede the shared name should concede a shared God — differing only in later 'corruptions' like the Trinity. On this footing Islam presents itself as the purification of Abrahamic monotheism rather than a rival deity's cult, and dawah regularly cites Arab Christian usage of 'Allah' as evidence that Islam worships the same God Christians do, merely more consistently.
rationale: Graded answered: the polemic's factual core is simply wrong, and Muslim (and Arab Christian) sources answer it decisively — 'Allah' predates Islam as the Arabic word for God, used in Christian inscriptions and every Arabic Bible. Christians who lead with it lose credibility with any Arabic-speaking hearer in the first minute. The entry's evangelistic value is triage: drop the lexical argument, keep the conceptual one. Whether the Quran's Allah — a non-triune monad who is not Father, has no Son, and saves without atonement — accurately describes the God of Abraham is the real question, and the app's doctrine-of-god and tahrif entries prosecute it on ground that actually holds.
